variants.title: Size the adapter
variants.context: For a frozen matrix W0 with shape d_out by d_in, the adapter factors are A (r by d_in) and B (d_out by r), so each adapted projection adds r(d_in + d_out) trainable parameters. Original LoRA scales the update by alpha / r, so changing rank with a fixed alpha also changes the scale.
variants.prompt: One 2,048 by 2,048 projection receives a rank-8 adapter. How many trainable parameters does that single projection add?
variants.hint: Add the two dimensions, then multiply by the rank.
variants.explanation: r(d_in + d_out) = 8 x (2,048 + 2,048) = 32,768 parameters for A and B together.

mistakes.feedback: That is the size of the frozen W0 itself; the adapter adds only r(d_in + d_out).
Add d_in and d_out before multiplying by r; 8 x 2,048 counts only one factor.

variants.title: Size the adapter
variants.context: For a frozen matrix W0 with shape d_out by d_in, the adapter factors are A (r by d_in) and B (d_out by r), so each adapted projection adds r(d_in + d_out) trainable parameters. Original LoRA scales the update by alpha / r, so changing rank with a fixed alpha also changes the scale.
variants.prompt: A 22-layer fixture has 2,048-wide hidden projections. LoRA rank 8 is applied to q_proj and v_proj in every layer. How many trainable adapter parameters are added in total?
variants.hint: Per projection, then per layer, then across layers.
variants.explanation: Each projection adds 8 x (2,048 + 2,048) = 32,768; times 2 projections times 22 layers = 1,441,792.

mistakes.feedback: Both q_proj and v_proj receive adapters; multiply by two projections per layer.
That is one projection in one layer; multiply by projections per layer and by layers.

variants.title: Size the adapter
variants.context: For a frozen matrix W0 with shape d_out by d_in, the adapter factors are A (r by d_in) and B (d_out by r), so each adapted projection adds r(d_in + d_out) trainable parameters. Original LoRA scales the update by alpha / r, so changing rank with a fixed alpha also changes the scale.
variants.prompt: A recipe keeps alpha at 32 while raising rank from 8 to 64 to add capacity. Under original LoRA scaling, what is the new update scale factor?
variants.hint: The scale is alpha divided by the new rank.
variants.explanation: alpha / r = 32 / 64 = 0.5, down from 32 / 8 = 4; rank and alpha are separate choices, so the scale moved too.

mistakes.feedback: That is the factor at rank 8; the rank changed.
The scale is alpha divided by r, not r divided by alpha.

variants.title: Trace the adapted layer
variants.context: One adapted linear layer sends the same activation x through the frozen base path W0 x and through the low-rank branch, where A compresses into r directions, B expands back to the output width, and the result is scaled by alpha / r before both paths are added. Only A and B are optimized; W0 is loaded but receives no updates.
variants.prompt: An activation enters an adapted q_proj during a forward pass. Put the steps in order.

items.text: B expands the r-dimensional result back to the output width.
The branch output is scaled by alpha divided by r.
The frozen matrix W0 transforms x without receiving gradients.
The activation x enters both the frozen base path and the low-rank branch.
A compresses x into r directions.
The base result and the scaled delta are added and passed to the downstream layer.

variants.hint: Compression comes before expansion, and scaling before the add.
variants.explanation: h = W0 x + (alpha / r) B A x: the base path and the scaled low-rank path meet at the layer output.

variants.title: Trace the adapted layer
variants.context: One adapted linear layer sends the same activation x through the frozen base path W0 x and through the low-rank branch, where A compresses into r directions, B expands back to the output width, and the result is scaled by alpha / r before both paths are added. Only A and B are optimized; W0 is loaded but receives no updates.
variants.prompt: A base model is wrapped with adapters whose B factor starts at zero. Put the events in order from wrapping to the first changed output.

items.text: The loss produces nonzero gradients for A and B while W0 stays frozen.
Wrap the target projections with A initialized randomly and B initialized to zero.
The optimizer updates B away from zero, and A along with it.
The first forward pass adds B A x, which is zero, so the output matches the base model exactly.
The next forward pass adds a nonzero scaled delta to W0 x.

variants.hint: Why does wrapping not change the output immediately?
variants.explanation: Zero-effect initialization makes the adapter a no-op at step zero; learning begins only once the optimizer moves B off zero.

variants.context: One adapted linear layer sends the same activation x through the frozen base path W0 x and through the low-rank branch, where A compresses into r directions, B expands back to the output width, and the result is scaled by alpha / r before both paths are added. Only A and B are optimized; W0 is loaded but receives no updates.
variants.prompt: A controlled build materializes a merged checkpoint from a trained adapter. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Add the scaled delta into W0 to form the merged weight for that projection.
Compute the scaled delta (alpha / r) B A for each adapted projection.
Load the exact base revision W0 that the adapter was trained against.
Evaluate, sign, and version the merged checkpoint as a complete model.

variants.hint: The merge is only meaningful against the base the adapter was trained on.
variants.explanation: Merging materializes W0 + delta W into a new full checkpoint that must then be released as a complete model.

variants.title: Build the adapter artifact
variants.context: A reproducible adapter artifact is built in five steps: freeze the task contract, pin model lineage, declare the recipe, train and inspect, then package the delta with its evidence, compatibility contract, rollback target, and integrity digest. Training loss alone does not prove the adapter generalizes or loads in production.
variants.prompt: A team starts its first LoRA adapter for a response-format task. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Train and inspect optimization, throughput, memory, task metrics, rare slices, safety, and regressions against the frozen base.
Declare the recipe: target modules, rank, alpha, dropout, initialization, quantization, compute dtype, optimizer, seed, and data manifest.
Package adapter weights, configuration, evidence, dependency versions, compatibility contract, rollback target, and integrity digest together.
Pin the immutable base revision, architecture, tokenizer files, special tokens, and template identity.
Freeze the task contract: prompt or chat template, output schema, rubric, holdout groups, critical slices, and baseline result.

variants.hint: Nothing is trained until the contract, lineage, and recipe are written down.
variants.explanation: Measure, identify, configure, learn, release: each step records what the next one depends on.

variants.title: Build the adapter artifact
variants.context: A reproducible adapter artifact is built in five steps: freeze the task contract, pin model lineage, declare the recipe, train and inspect, then package the delta with its evidence, compatibility contract, rollback target, and integrity digest. Training loss alone does not prove the adapter generalizes or loads in production.
variants.prompt: A new immutable base revision arrives after an adapter has shipped. Put the steps needed to re-establish a valid artifact in order.

items.text: Re-run the release evidence before the runtime accepts the new base-plus-adapter pair.
Pin the new base revision, tokenizer files, special tokens, and template identity.
Package the new delta with its compatibility contract, rollback target, and digest.
Retrain and inspect task, slice, safety, and regression metrics against the new frozen base.
Re-declare the recipe against the new base with target modules, rank, alpha, seed, and data manifest.

variants.hint: Which step of the five is unchanged when only the base moves?
variants.explanation: Release evidence is re-run whenever the base revision changes; the task contract can stay, but lineage, recipe, training, and packaging repeat.

variants.title: Build the adapter artifact
variants.context: A reproducible adapter artifact is built in five steps: freeze the task contract, pin model lineage, declare the recipe, train and inspect, then package the delta with its evidence, compatibility contract, rollback target, and integrity digest. Training loss alone does not prove the adapter generalizes or loads in production.
variants.prompt: A QLoRA run is planned because the frozen base does not fit in memory at BF16. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Package the delta and confirm the runtime supports its format, target modules, dtype, and quantized path.
Freeze the task contract with holdout groups, critical slices, and the baseline result.
Train and inspect memory, throughput, task metrics, and regressions against the frozen base.
Declare NF4 quantization, double quantization, paged optimizers, and the compute dtype in the recipe.
Pin the base revision, tokenizer, and template identity.

variants.hint: Quantization is part of the declared recipe, not a runtime surprise.
variants.explanation: QLoRA changes the recipe and the compatibility contract; a 4-bit checkpoint is not evidence that quality matches a higher-precision baseline.

variants.title: Change one capacity decision
variants.context: Rank controls the bottleneck width, target modules control where change is allowed, and alpha controls update scale through alpha / r. Change one decision at a time: increase rank only when a lower-rank run underfits and data or target-module coverage is not the real bottleneck, and do not read a larger adapter as automatically better.
variants.prompt: A rank-8 adapter on q_proj and v_proj underfits. Data coverage has been audited as sufficient. Which single change is the best next hypothesis?
options: Raise rank and alpha together and broaden modules in one run.
Raise rank to 64 on the same two projections.
Broaden the target modules at the same rank before touching rank.
optionFeedback: Changing several capacity decisions at once hides which one mattered.
Rank widens the bottleneck, but the update stays confined to two attention projections that may be the real limit.
Target-module coverage must be ruled out as the bottleneck before rank is increased.
variants.hint: What must be ruled out before rank goes up?
variants.explanation: Increase rank only when the lower-rank run underfits and data or target-module coverage is not the actual bottleneck.

variants.title: Change one capacity decision
variants.context: Rank controls the bottleneck width, target modules control where change is allowed, and alpha controls update scale through alpha / r. Change one decision at a time: increase rank only when a lower-rank run underfits and data or target-module coverage is not the real bottleneck, and do not read a larger adapter as automatically better.
variants.prompt: To fix underfitting, a team raises rank from 8 to 32 and keeps alpha at 16. Held-out quality gets worse. What changed besides capacity?
options: Nothing; rank was the only variable in the run.
The update scale fell from 2 to 0.5 because alpha / r changed.
The target modules narrowed when the rank changed.
optionFeedback: Rank and alpha are separate choices, but the scale depends on both.
Original LoRA applies alpha / r; a fixed alpha with a quadrupled rank cuts the update scale to a quarter.
Target modules do not move when rank moves.
variants.hint: What is the scale factor before and after?
variants.explanation: Rank, alpha, initialization, learning rate, and target modules are a jointly versioned recipe; changing rank alone changes the scale.

variants.title: Change one capacity decision
variants.context: Rank controls the bottleneck width, target modules control where change is allowed, and alpha controls update scale through alpha / r. Change one decision at a time: increase rank only when a lower-rank run underfits and data or target-module coverage is not the real bottleneck, and do not read a larger adapter as automatically better.
variants.prompt: A rank-128 adapter on all linear layers matches a rank-16 attention adapter on aggregate quality but trains less stably and memorizes a noisy slice. What should the team conclude?
options: Keep the smaller adapter; extra capacity is memorizing noise without a measured gain.
Raise the learning rate so the larger adapter converges more cleanly.
Ship the larger adapter; more capacity is the safer default.
optionFeedback: Extra capacity can memorize noise or make optimization less stable, and here it bought nothing.
Learning rate is another capacity-adjacent choice; changing it now confounds the comparison.
A larger adapter is not automatically better.
variants.hint: What did the extra parameters buy on the held-out metrics?
variants.explanation: Do not interpret a larger adapter as automatically better; compare held-out task and slice metrics and keep the smaller recipe when they tie.

variants.title: Choose the deployment boundary
variants.context: Dynamic adapters keep one frozen base and activate a named adapter per request or tenant. A merged checkpoint materializes W0 + delta W into a new full artifact that must be evaluated, signed, distributed, and rolled back as a complete model. Combined adapters need their own evaluation, and no mode frees an adapter from its training lineage.
variants.prompt: A platform serves forty tenant-specific behaviors on one base model and must switch between them per request. Which boundary fits?
options: Dynamic adapters activated per request on one resident base.
Forty merged checkpoints, one full model per tenant.
One combined adapter merged from all forty tenant adapters.
optionFeedback: Dynamic loading avoids duplicated base storage and keeps adapter rollback independent of the base.
Forty full checkpoints multiply storage, evaluation, signing, and rollback cost.
Never assume individually good adapters remain good after combination; tenants also need isolation.
variants.hint: Which mode keeps one base resident and swaps behaviors cheaply?
variants.explanation: Dynamic adapters make routing, cache residency, and tenant isolation part of the serving design in exchange for one shared base.

variants.title: Choose the deployment boundary
variants.context: Dynamic adapters keep one frozen base and activate a named adapter per request or tenant. A merged checkpoint materializes W0 + delta W into a new full artifact that must be evaluated, signed, distributed, and rolled back as a complete model. Combined adapters need their own evaluation, and no mode frees an adapter from its training lineage.
variants.prompt: A single-purpose service wants the simplest inference path and never swaps adapters, so it plans to merge. What does merging cost it?
options: Nothing beyond build time; merging only removes the runtime adapter branch.
Cheap adapter swapping, plus a larger artifact that is evaluated, signed, and rolled back as a complete model.
The tokenizer and template lineage, which a merged model no longer needs.
optionFeedback: Merging produces a larger artifact that carries full-model release obligations.
That is the trade: a simpler serving path in exchange for a heavier release artifact and no cheap swapping.
Merging changes packaging, not the need for lineage.
variants.hint: What becomes a full-model responsibility after the merge?
variants.explanation: A merged checkpoint removes the adapter branch but must be evaluated, signed, distributed, and rolled back as a complete model.

variants.prompt: The runtime loads a shipped adapter against base revision v2, which has the same hidden size as the v1 revision the adapter was trained on. What should the compatibility gate do?
options: Accept the pair; the dimensions match.
Reject the pair; the adapter is a delta against exactly revision v1.
Accept after merging, since a merge removes the base dependency.
optionFeedback: Reject a different base revision even when dimensions appear similar.
The adapter is a versioned delta against one exact base and input-format contract.
Merging changes packaging, not lineage; the merge itself must use the exact base.
variants.hint: Does matching shape mean matching weights?
variants.explanation: An adapter is a versioned delta against one exact base revision, tokenizer, and template; a different revision is rejected regardless of shape.
